channel.title: Diurna — The Iran war
channel.description: Diurna’s day-by-day coverage: The Iran war.

item.title: Qatar seals a defence pact with Turkey as Israel debates a strike on Iran
item.description:
Doha and Ankara pledged on Friday to stand together against any armed attack on either of them, a sign of waning faith in America’s guarantees in the Gulf. In Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government is preparing a fresh offensive against Iran, without open backing from the army or Washington.

In Istanbul on Friday 13 November, Turkey’s president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and the emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, signed a mutual-defence agreement under which the two countries promise a common stance against any external armed attack, Al Jazeera reports. Gulf monarchies believe America’s security guarantees no longer work, according to a Turkish analyst quoted by the channel, as the Revolutionary Guards’ navy says an LNG tanker struck a mine in Hormuz and America’s military command says it shot down two Iranian drones heading for Bahrain. In Israel, the security cabinet chaired by the outgoing prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered faster preparations for an attack on Iran, according to Israeli media, though the general staff sees no urgency and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next government, fears “devastating” consequences.

item.title: Iran says it hit an American radar in Bahrain as Donald Trump rules out a deal
item.description:
The Revolutionary Guards claim to have destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday in retaliation for a strike on the port of Sirik, a claim America’s military disputes. A day earlier America’s president called a deal with Tehran unnecessary and took his vice-president off the file.

On Thursday 12 November Donald Trump wrote that America did “not need a deal with Iran” and told his vice-president, JD Vance, who had been considering a meeting with the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, to focus on crime in Democratic-run cities, Middle East Eye reports. The reversal, days after he spoke of “momentum” towards a settlement, comes as Tehran denies any planned meeting in Qatar, refuses to send its enriched uranium abroad and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed until its conditions are met. On Friday 13 November the Revolutionary Guards said they had destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an unclaimed strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik, on the Strait of Hormuz, while America’s Central Command says it shot down two drones, causing no damage, according to RFE/RL and Fox News.

item.title: Israel is reportedly readying a strike on Iran as two supertankers explode in Hormuz
item.description:
Israel’s security cabinet has reportedly ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack, according to the public broadcaster Kan. In Hormuz, the Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers were disabled by explosions.

On the evening of Wednesday 11 November Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack on Iran, according to the public broadcaster Kan, cited by Al Jazeera, even as Gadi Eisenkot urged him not to deploy the army without a direct and immediate threat. That same night two supertankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings, the Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday, threatening the same fate for any ship that co-operates with the American armed forces, according to Reuters. Donald Trump says he is ready to return to war if Qatar’s mediation fails, even though his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, thinks the blockade effective enough to make that unnecessary, and Brent closed at $92.76 on Wednesday after Tehran rejected moving its enriched uranium to a third country, according to Al Jazeera.

item.title: France accuses Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of sabotaging the fridges of 700 shops
item.description:
France’s foreign minister blames a cyber unit linked to the Guards for the attack on supermarkets on 12 October. Iran’s ambassador has been summoned and Paris wants European sanctions.

On Monday 9 November France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, blamed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for the cyber-attack which, on the night of 11-12 October, tampered with refrigeration in some 700 French shops, including Carrefour, Monoprix, Intermarché and Coopérative U stores. According to ANSSI, France’s national cyber-security agency, the attack was the work of Shahid Kaveh, a unit linked to the Guards and betrayed by traces of Persian and Iranian IP addresses, and temperatures rose as high as 50°C for about six hours, the AP reports. Paris has summoned Iran’s ambassador and wants European sanctions, which EU foreign ministers could discuss on 16 November, while Tehran dismisses the accusations as “baseless and biased”.

item.title: Iran lifts the range limit on its missiles after fresh American strikes in Hormuz
item.description:
The Revolutionary Guards say they no longer observe a 2,000km ceiling on their ballistic missiles. Washington has set up a force to hunt down Iranian arms smuggling, as advisers urge Donald Trump to resume the war.

On Saturday 7 November the spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, General Hossein Mohebbi, said in Tehran that the 2,000km limit Iran had imposed on the range of its ballistic missiles had been lifted, a day after American strikes on air defences on Qeshm island. The announcement, which does not say whether Iran already has longer-range missiles, came alongside a statement attributed to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, promising a response “without geographical limits” to any American or Israeli threat. According to NBC, advisers have urged Donald Trump to resume large-scale operations before the new Congress sits in January, and America’s Central Command has announced a force to cut the land and Caspian routes by which Iran obtains weapons.

item.title: America strikes Iranian air defences in the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran vows to respond
item.description:
Donald Trump confirmed on Friday evening “minor” strikes on an anti-aircraft system on Qeshm island, where Tehran says it shot down an American drone. Iran’s army promises an “immediate” response, while Qatar denies that negotiations have failed.

On Friday 6 November Donald Trump confirmed that American forces had carried out what he called “minor” strikes on an air-defence system on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian state media reported two explosions and where Tehran says it shot down an American drone. The strikes, the first since the Republicans’ defeat in the midterm elections, which the president blames on the war, come as he speaks both of “progress” with Tehran and of possibly destroying “the rest of Iran”, while Qatar, the mediator, denies that negotiations have failed. On Saturday the Iranian army’s spokesman, Mohammad Akraminia, promised an “immediate” response without geographical limits on the supreme leader’s orders, while Tehran still insists that its conditions, including an end to the American blockade and to sanctions, be met before any nuclear talks.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

item.title: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
item.description:
Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.

On Thursday 5 November Iranian forces reported at least five tankers and a tugboat ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, most of them after striking mines on routes Tehran had not authorised; Britain’s UKMTO agency also reported a vessel hit by two projectiles north of Qatar. The same day, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had sent Washington, through Qatar, a proposal on its nuclear programme, to be discussed only once seven demands are met, among them the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets and war reparations. The United States, which is studying the text, wants the nuclear issue on the table from the outset, and thousands of American troops stand ready to resume fighting, according to the New York Times, just as several of Donald Trump’s allies distance themselves from the war after the defeat of 3 November.

item.title: Washington and Tehran: fears of a return to war after the US vote
item.description:
Qatar is trying to secure an interim deal before the United States resumes its strikes. Eight months into the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains almost closed and oil is above $100 a barrel.

After three days of talks in Doha, the Iranian delegation returned to Tehran without a deal, and messages between the two capitals now pass only through the Qatari mediator. The two sides remain far apart: Washington wants commitments on Iran’s nuclear programme before making any concession, while Tehran makes reopening the Strait of Hormuz conditional on lifting oil sanctions, unfreezing its assets abroad and ending the fighting in Lebanon. American strikes have never fully stopped: the island of Qeshm was hit again on 2 November, and Donald Trump, who had promised not to launch a new offensive before the elections, has not ruled out further operations.
